findings.summary: `*` and `+` empty bullets also now interrupt paragraphs, making a literal lone `*`/`+` line disappear into a bullet
findings.evidence:
`isEmptyBulletLine` accepts `-`, `*` and `+`. Upstream, a paragraph line followed by a lone `*` (or `+`) is a lazy continuation and the character is rendered as literal text (`

some text
*

`); the `lheading` ambiguity that motivated #517 exists only for `-`. With `wrappedList` returning true for any empty bullet, `some text\n*\nmore` now terminates the paragraph, turns the `*` into an empty `
  • ` and splits `more` into a separate block, so the user's literal `*` glyph vanishes from the rendered output. Only the `-` case is required by the issue and covered by tests.

findings.summary: Plugin reads markdown-it's private `__rules__`; a shape change throws at module-import time and takes down the whole preview
findings.evidence: `getRuleFn` does `ruler.__rules__.find(...)` and `throw new Error('markdown-it block rule not found: list')` if absent. This runs synchronously from `md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)` at module scope in preview.ts:48, so any markdown-it upgrade/refactor that renames or restructures the private registry converts a rendering nit into an uncaught exception during import of `preview.ts`, breaking the entire notes preview rather than degrading it. `md.block.ruler.getRules('paragraph')` / a `try`+fallback (leave the stock rule in place) would fail soft.

findings.summary: `wrappedList` silent short-circuit omits the >=4-indent code-block guard the real `list` rule has
findings.evidence: `isEmptyBulletLine` only checks `state.sCount[line] < state.blkIndent`; the real `list` rule additionally returns false when `state.sCount[startLine] - state.blkIndent >= 4` (indented code). So `wrappedList` can claim to terminate a paragraph on a line the stock rule would reject. Today all callers of paragraph-terminator rules (`rules_block/paragraph` and this file's `lheading` copy) `continue` past lines with `sCount - blkIndent > 3`, so it is currently unreachable — but the guard is missing and any future terminator caller (or a plugin registered with `alt: ['paragraph']` that scans without that skip) would terminate a paragraph and reinterpret an indented-code line as a list.

findings.summary: Setext heading content trimmed with an ASCII-only regex where upstream uses `String.prototype.trim()`
findings.evidence: markdown-it 14.x `rules_block/lheading.mjs` computes `state.getLines(...).trim()`. The copy uses `asciiTrim()` (only \\x09-\\x0d and space), so a heading whose text is padded with non-ASCII whitespace (e.g. U+00A0, U+2003) keeps that whitespace inside the `<h1>/<h2>` inline content where stock markdown-it would strip it. Divergence is small but the rule is billed as a drop-in mirror.

findings.summary: Fix is applied globally, not scoped to the list context the issue describes — it also breaks valid top-level single-dash setext headings
findings.evidence: `const isLoneDash = marker === DASH && runLength === 1;` unconditionally disqualifies a lone `-` as a setext underline anywhere in the document, including outside any list (`Heading\n-` at blkIndent 0, which is valid CommonMark H2 and is what GitHub renders). The issue #517 outcome only asks that a *nested empty bullet under a list item* stop turning its parent into an `<h2>`; nothing in it asks to change top-level setext parsing. The guard could have been conditioned on `state.blkIndent > 0` / list parent type. The design-doc note (docs/design/notes/notes.md:296-299) claims "Multi-dash `---` and `=` setext underlines are untouched" but does not acknowledge that single-dash setext headings — the common `Heading` + `-` form — now silently stop being headings everywhere in a note.

findings.summary: Approach couples the notes preview to markdown-it internals: a vendored copy of the upstream `lheading` rule plus a private `__rules__` read
findings.evidence: `getRuleFn` reads `md.block.ruler as unknown as { __rules__: ... }` (an undocumented private registry, guarded only by a throw), and `lheadingRule` is a ~70-line verbatim fork of markdown-it 14.x `rules_block/lheading.mjs` that must be re-synced on every markdown-it upgrade. The sibling `details-plugin.ts` achieves its extension purely through the public `md.block.ruler.before(...)` API. A narrower approach — registering a new terminator rule before `lheading`/`list` with `alt: ['paragraph']` rather than replacing and delegating to the stock rules — would avoid both the fork and the private access. Fit/maintenance concern, not a correctness claim.

findings.summary: Scope creep beyond the issue: `*` and `+` empty bullets are also given paragraph-interrupting power
findings.evidence: `isEmptyBulletLine` accepts `*` (0x2a) and `+` (0x2b) as well as `-`. Those markers have no setext ambiguity, so they were never part of issue #517's failure mode; relaxing the CommonMark "an empty list item cannot interrupt a paragraph" rule for them is an additional, unrequested deviation from CommonMark (`* 1\n  *` previously rendered as lazy text). Arguably consistent, but it widens the notes-only spec deviation beyond what the issue asked for and is not called out in the design-doc note.

findings.summary: Design note added under "P2 — Feature parity / Later Phases (sketch)" rather than with the preview-rendering behavior it documents
findings.evidence: The new `#### Empty nested bullet vs setext heading — shipped (issue #517)` section sits inside the `### P2 — Feature parity` block of the "Later Phases (sketch)" section, next to the details-plugin note. It follows the existing precedent in this file (details-plugin is filed the same way) and is folded into the canonical notes doc rather than a parallel file, which satisfies the design-doc discipline rule; the placement under a "sketch" heading for shipped preview behavior is only a taste issue.

findings.summary: Deviation applies only to the preview pane; the CodeMirror source editor's markdown highlighting still treats the lone `-` as a setext underline
findings.evidence: `listEmptyBulletPlugin` is registered only on the preview's `MarkdownIt` instance. The notes editor uses `@codemirror/lang-markdown` (docs/design/notes/notes.md:113-116), which parses CommonMark independently, so `- 1\n  -` may still be styled as a heading in the source pane while the preview no longer is — the two panes now disagree. The issue's screenshot appears to be the preview, so this may be acceptable, but the design note does not record the divergence.

findings.summary: The wholesale reimplementation of `lheading` is only covered for the `---` case; `=` (h1) underlines and its paragraph-terminator/indent branches are untested
findings.evidence: lheadingRule is a hand-copied replacement for the upstream rule including the `EQUALS` branch (level 1), the >=4-space indent bail (line 74), the lazy-continuation `continue` (line 86), the terminator-rule loop (line 119-126) and a re-implemented `asciiTrim` (line 19-23). The only test of the replaced rule is `Heading\n---` (preview.test.ts:182). No test renders `Heading\n===` into `<h1>`, no test covers a multi-line paragraph with a setext underline (which is what exercises `asciiTrim`/`getLines`), and no test covers the indented-code bail. A transcription error in any of those branches ships silently.

findings.summary: The trailing-space and blank-line tests assert only selector existence, not that the nested item is empty
findings.evidence: Both `nests an empty bullet with a trailing space too` (line 168-173) and `still renders the blank-line workaround correctly` (line 175-180) assert only `querySelector('ul > li > ul > li')` is truthy plus no `<h2>`. They would pass even if the nested item wrongly contained the parent's text. The first test (line 153) does check emptiness; these two are weaker duplicates of it.

findings.summary: CodeMirror's `markdown()` parser in the notes editor still follows CommonMark, so the editor and the preview now disagree about a lone `-`
findings.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:200 configures the editor with `markdown()` from `@codemirror/lang-markdown` (lezer-markdown, strict CommonMark). That parser still treats a lone `-` after a text line as a setext underline and highlights the line above as a heading, while `md.render` (preview.ts:165, now using listEmptyBulletPlugin) renders it as a paragraph plus an empty nested bullet. The same note therefore gets heading styling in the left pane and list rendering in the right pane. The plugin is preview-only; nothing was changed on the editor side to match. Fix likely belongs in editor.ts (markdown-parser config) or is an accepted divergence that should be recorded.

findings.summary: The lheading replacement changes rendering of ALL existing note content that uses a single-dash setext H2 (`Title\n-`), not just the nested-empty-bullet case
findings.evidence:
The `isLoneDash` guard in list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:105 is unconditional — it applies at document top level, not only inside a list. `Title\n-` is a valid CommonMark H2 and previously rendered as `

Title

` through the shared `md` instance (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:165, used by every note via editor.ts:117). After this change it renders as a paragraph followed by an empty `
  • `, silently altering already-stored notes that used the shorthand underline. docs/design/notes/notes.md:297 only states that multi-dash `---` and `=` underlines are untouched; the todo (docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-todo.md:62) even listed a "top-level lone dash" test that was not added, so this consumer-visible change is uncovered.

findings.summary: Hand-rolled `asciiTrim` uses a quadratic backtracking trim regex on attacker-controllable note content (ReDoS → preview/tab hang)
findings.evidence:
`ASCII_TRIM_RE = /^[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+|[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+$/g` (line 19-20) is the textbook quadratic "trim" pattern (same shape as the `/^\s+|\s+$/g` ReDoS in CVE-2021-33623 / trim-newlines). The unanchored second alternative `[ws]+$` is retried at every offset inside a whitespace run and backtracks one char at a time when the run is not followed by end-of-string, giving O(n²) work.

Vector: it is applied at line 134-136 to `state.getLines(startLine, nextLine, ...)` — i.e. raw setext-heading paragraph text straight from note source. A collaborator (notes content is shared via Yorkie and rendered into every other member's preview) writes a note containing:

    a<200_000 spaces>b
    ===

The heading branch is taken, `asciiTrim` is called on `"a" + 200k spaces + "b\n"`, and because the space run is followed by `b` (not by end-of-string) the engine backtracks the whole run at each of ~200k start offsets ≈ 2e10 steps — the render call hangs the main thread. `packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:165` (`this.el.innerHTML = md.render(markdown)`) is synchronous, and `packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:150` (`renderPreview`) re-runs it on every document change, so the hang is re-triggered on each edit/remote patch, freezing the victim's tab (no way to type the content back out). Upstream markdown-it's `lheading` uses native `String.prototype.trim()` (linear), so this quadratic scan is introduced by this change. Fix: use `.trim()`, or a linear two-pointer/anchored-alternative trim (`/^[ws]+/` then `/[ws]+$/` with a lastIndex-style scan) instead of one global alternation.

findings.summary: `Ruler.at('list', ...)` captures the `list` fn eagerly and hardcodes its `alt` chain, silently swallowing any later plugin's `list` override or added terminator membership
findings.evidence: `originalList = getRuleFn(md, 'list')` (line 179) snapshots whatever `list` implementation exists at registration time, and line 197-199 re-registers the wrapper with a hardcoded `alt: ['paragraph','reference','blockquote']`. Any plugin applied to this shared `md` singleton *after* `listEmptyBulletPlugin` (preview.ts:48 is currently last, but detailsPlugin already registers a paragraph/list terminator at details-plugin.ts:104) that itself wraps `list` would be silently discarded on the empty-bullet path, and any `alt` membership another plugin had added to `list` is dropped. If a future plugin's `list` wrapper carries a containment/escaping concern, the bypass would read as covered. I could not identify a currently-shipping plugin whose behavior is lost, so confidence is low; hardening = read the rule fn lazily inside the wrapper and preserve the existing `alt` array rather than a literal.

verdict.reason:
The code is present as described — `list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:105` guards on dash-run length only, with no list-context condition, and `wrappedList` (:181-193) fires for any empty bullet terminating a paragraph, so top-level `Title\n-` does render as `

` + empty `

  • ` rather than `

    `. However, this is the explicitly specified intent, not a logic error: docs/design/notes/notes.md:293-299 states the deviation is that "a **lone single `-`** (the empty-bullet shape) is **never** a setext underline, and an empty bullet is allowed to interrupt a paragraph", with only multi-dash `---` and `=` underlines preserved — deliberately scoped by dash-run length, not by list context, exactly as implemented. The effect is also confined to the notes preview renderer: the plugin is registered only on the single module-level markdown-it instance at packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:48 and nowhere else in the repo, and it changes render output only — the stored markdown source is never modified, so there is no crash, no data loss, no broken invariant, and no async/state defect. What remains is a design-scope disagreement about how narrow the deliberate CommonMark deviation should be (the reviewer's own suggested fix is a scoping preference, and they concede "this may be intentional"), which belongs to the architecture/design lens, not the Correctness lens whose rubric covers wrong conditions, boundary errors, missing-guard crashes, data loss and async mistakes.

samples.summary: Hand-rolled `asciiTrim` uses a quadratic backtracking trim regex on attacker-controllable note content (ReDoS → preview/tab hang)
samples.evidence:
`ASCII_TRIM_RE = /^[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+|[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+$/g` (line 19-20) is the textbook quadratic "trim" pattern (same shape as the `/^\s+|\s+$/g` ReDoS in CVE-2021-33623 / trim-newlines). The unanchored second alternative `[ws]+$` is retried at every offset inside a whitespace run and backtracks one char at a time when the run is not followed by end-of-string, giving O(n²) work.

Vector: it is applied at line 134-136 to `state.getLines(startLine, nextLine, ...)` — i.e. raw setext-heading paragraph text straight from note source. A collaborator (notes content is shared via Yorkie and rendered into every other member's preview) writes a note containing:

    a<200_000 spaces>b
    ===

The heading branch is taken, `asciiTrim` is called on `"a" + 200k spaces + "b\n"`, and because the space run is followed by `b` (not by end-of-string) the engine backtracks the whole run at each of ~200k start offsets ≈ 2e10 steps — the render call hangs the main thread. `packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:165` (`this.el.innerHTML = md.render(markdown)`) is synchronous, and `packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:150` (`renderPreview`) re-runs it on every document change, so the hang is re-triggered on each edit/remote patch, freezing the victim's tab (no way to type the content back out). Upstream markdown-it's `lheading` uses native `String.prototype.trim()` (linear), so this quadratic scan is introduced by this change. Fix: use `.trim()`, or a linear two-pointer/anchored-alternative trim (`/^[ws]+/` then `/[ws]+$/` with a lastIndex-style scan) instead of one global alternation.

samples.summary: `Ruler.at('list', ...)` captures the `list` fn eagerly and hardcodes its `alt` chain, silently swallowing any later plugin's `list` override or added terminator membership
samples.evidence: `originalList = getRuleFn(md, 'list')` (line 179) snapshots whatever `list` implementation exists at registration time, and line 197-199 re-registers the wrapper with a hardcoded `alt: ['paragraph','reference','blockquote']`. Any plugin applied to this shared `md` singleton *after* `listEmptyBulletPlugin` (preview.ts:48 is currently last, but detailsPlugin already registers a paragraph/list terminator at details-plugin.ts:104) that itself wraps `list` would be silently discarded on the empty-bullet path, and any `alt` membership another plugin had added to `list` is dropped. If a future plugin's `list` wrapper carries a containment/escaping concern, the bypass would read as covered. I could not identify a currently-shipping plugin whose behavior is lost, so confidence is low; hardening = read the rule fn lazily inside the wrapper and preserve the existing `alt` array rather than a literal.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate in every checkable respect. `ASCII_TRIM_RE = /^[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+|[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+$/g` exists verbatim at list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:19-20 and is applied via `asciiTrim` at line 134-136 to `state.getLines(...)`, i.e. raw note source for a setext-heading paragraph. The second alternative `[ws]+$` is unanchored, so with the /g flag the engine retries at every offset inside a whitespace run and, when the run is followed by a non-whitespace char (never satisfying `$`), backtracks one character at a time — the canonical O(n^2) trim ReDoS (same shape as CVE-2021-33623). I searched packages/notes/src for any length cap, truncation, timeout, or worker isolation guarding `md.render` and found none, so no `already-guarded` ground applies. I considered `out-of-scope` on lane fit (ReDoS is not an explicitly enumerated category) but rejected it: it is untrusted-input handling with a cross-user impact (one collaborator can freeze another's tab, with no way for the victim to edit the payload back out), which is a genuine security weakness rather than a pure correctness bug.
